text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-For the second time in seven months French President Jacques Chirac in Beirut.
-President Elias Hrawi nominated Rafik al-Hariri as a prime minister for the third time.
-U.S. charge d'affaires Ron Shleiker says there is no contradiction between the French and the American roles in the Middle East.
-European Investment Bank awards $63-million soft loan to Lebanon for environmental projects.
-Guerrillas launch series of attacks against pro-Israeli militia positions in south Lebanon, wounding one militiaman.
-Speaker of the Parliament Nabih Berri says the containers of industrial toxic wastes found in Beirut port are connected to administrative corruption.
-Military appeals court confirmed the death sentence on a Moslem guerrilla for the 1986 murder of a French military attache but commuted it to life imprisonment.
-Chairman of the rightwing Falange Party George Sa'adeh withdrew his resignation.
Syrian President Assad held talks with Lebanese Prime Minister Hariri in Damascus.
